notes:
Topline: mid-market product analytics SaaS evaluating Redwood as migration path from current LLM-provider (mostly OpenAI). Looking to start on Hosted API to validate parity and infra before moving to Dedicated (VPC + reserved GPUs) for production. Key asks: 1) prompt parity — must match existing responses for NPS/summary flows; 2) regressions detection — need automated eval harness and alerting; 3) predictable unit cost and routing fallbacks.

What they currently run: proprietary prompt templates + OpenAI chat models; custom post-processing to normalize outputs. Wants compatibility layer or guidance for model tokenization/stop sequences and sampling parameters. Concern about deterministic regressions when switching models/quantization.

Requirements discussed in calls:
- Latency target: p95 < 250ms for short chat completions (<=128 tokens) and < 800ms for product summary generation (<=600 tokens)
- Throughput: ~600 concurrent requests at peak, burst to 1k for launches
- Cost sensitivity: strong — aiming for < $0.03 per 1k tokens effective cost after optimizations
- Data residency: user data at rest in US only for now; Dedicated VPC preferred for Q3 production cutover
- Security: SSO (SAML), SOC2 compliance, audit logs, KMS integration

Migration plan (proposed):
- Phase 1: Hosted POC (2 weeks) — import prompts, run side-by-side evaluation vs current provider on 2k canonical prompts (scored) — produce regression delta report
- Phase 2: Extended validation (4 weeks) — add long-form summarization and code-assist prompts, stress tests for batching and KV cache behavior
- Phase 3: Dedicated sizing and legal + procurement, target Dedicated go-live in Q3 after SOC2/contract

Quotes / paraphrases:
- "We need parity on the summary prompt — even small hallucination differences cause product churn." — VP Product
- "If you can show predictable cost reductions without visible regressions, procurement will greenlight Dedicated." — Head of Engineering

Open items / next steps:

- Signalscale to share canonical prompt set + scoring rubric (action: Signalscale eng)
